title: Topic 5.4: Alcohol, Drugs and Substance Abuse

pages.lesson:
LESSON: ALCOHOL, DRUGS AND SUBSTANCE ABUSE

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Christian Living
Topic 5.4: Alcohol, Drugs and Substance Abuse

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Alcohol, Drugs and Substance Abuse. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do young people abuse alcohol and drugs?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain Christian teachings on the dangers of alcohol, drugs and substance abuse

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ALCOHOL, DRUGS AND SUBSTANCE ABUSE
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Alcohol, Drugs and Substance Abuse helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: ALCOHOL, DRUGS AND SUBSTANCE ABUSE
Study Alcohol, Drugs and Substance Abuse like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain Christian teachings on the dangers of alcohol, drugs and substance abuse

What this means
In this part you learn to explain Christian teachings on the dangers of alcohol, drugs and substance abuse. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain Christian teachings on the dangers of alcohol, drugs and substance abuse.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Alcohol, Drugs and Substance Abuse” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain Christian teachings on the dangers of alcohol, drugs and substance abuse. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Alcohol, Drugs and Substance Abuse is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Alcohol, Drugs and Substance Abuse” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain Christian teachings on the dangers of alcohol, drugs and substance abuse)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Alcohol, Drugs and Substance Abuse to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain Christian teachings on the dangers of alcohol, drugs and substance abuse.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Alcohol, Drugs and Substance Abuse from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Alcohol, Drugs and Substance Abuse: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Alcohol, Drugs and Substance Abuse?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do young people abuse alcohol and drugs?
2. How can you avoid alcohol, drugs and substance abuse?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Alcohol, Drugs and Substance Abuse means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain Christian teachings on the dangers of alcohol, drugs and substance abuse.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
